scope: Bounded read-only protocol/data source audit; not exhaustive coverage or candidate qualification
method: Read immutable Git objects, existing NC01–12 inventory and bounded existing-issue search. No tests, queues, deployments, source or issue mutations.

strong_existing_coverage.assertions: Mutation add/update/delete and rejected writes independently read stored state. Query service predicates test contradictory intersections.

Stored Z survives query only when requested; replica extract/sync checks literal XY/Z/M and spatial reference against authored values. True-curve input test explicitly asserts documented densification, not lossless curve output.

Microsoft.OData.Client exact filtered ID and disjoint pages; exact count/top/empty-boundary cases. Real Postgres component fixture tests stale PATCH ETag with persisted final value, atomic batch rollback and missing deleted entity.

Exact filtered IDs and numberMatched; full one-row page walk union/uniqueness and final empty page; property whitelist excludes unselected fields. Mutation ETag and geometry-preservation cases exist, alongside media/error tests.

Real HTTP/PostGIS mutation readback and invalid-write preservation; auth tests exercise production dispatcher/edit pipeline with only principal grants controlled. OWSLib exact numeric filter names/count, property projection, hits without members, page count/uniqueness, authored anchor and bbox-axis parity.
OWSLib parses capabilities; compares explicit EPSG4326/CRS84 wire and normalized bbox axes, equal rendered pixels, backgrounds, multilayer increased content and distant-bbox emptiness.

OWSLib checks grid geometry, matrix limits, REST/KVP equality, deterministic bytes and empty-data tiles. Separate .NET test requires actual red pixels from configured seed/style; protocol auth denies tile bytes to a principal lacking the read role.

findings.title: OWSLib transport probes cannot run against HTTPS despite documenting the same release lane
findings.evidence: WFS/WMS/WMTS each assert scheme == http before a branch that would record HTTPS pass. HTTPS necessarily fails; compose records not-applicable and cannot establish live TLS.
findings.recommendation: Retain explicit compose applicability, add a real HTTPS canonical-client request/certificate-validation path and typed refusal controls; do not relabel HTTP as TLS proof.

findings.title: OWSLib WMTS positive rendering receipt accepts a correctly sized blank PNG
findings.evidence: CERT-RNDR-01, zoom sweep and second grid assert only PNG decoding/dimensions. Always-transparent positive responses satisfy these checks, while the explicit distant tile emptiness check also passes. Separate .NET red-pixel integration exists, so this is a canonical-client receipt weakness, not missing server rendering coverage.
findings.recommendation: Require authored feature/style pixels at independently computed positions for positive tiles, distinguish both grids, retain a distant blank tile and add blank/wrong-location negative controls.

findings.title: OWSLib WMTS AUTH receipts substantiate an admin route rather than protected tile access
findings.evidence: WMTS AUTH01/02 use shared admin_probe and explicitly state the WMTS fixture is anonymous. The separate expanded canonical auth suite enumerates only OGC Features/WFS/WMS. .NET WMTS denied-no-payload/allowed-image proof exists and must be credited separately.
findings.recommendation: Exercise OWSLib against a genuinely protected WMTS tile through valid/invalid/expired credentials, assert challenge + absence of image bytes on denial and expected pixels on success; preserve existing generic admin checks as distinct evidence.

findings.title: Generic Python FeatureServer filter cases often assert only HTTP200
findings.evidence: Equality/inequality/range/LIKE/IN/BETWEEN/IS NULL/AND/OR cases do not inspect result rows. Ignored filters or universally empty successful responses can satisfy these individual cases. Other .NET predicate/state tests provide stronger independent coverage.
findings.recommendation: Use authored contrasting/null/boundary rows and assert exact expected ID sets, positive cardinality, exclusions and empty-result cases. Do not count these HTTP-only cases as semantic filter proof.

findings.title: GDAL WFS client filter and positive bbox checks allow over-return
findings.evidence: Raw WFS filter independently checks exactly alpha, but the actual ogr2ogr -where path checks only alpha membership. Its positive -spat path checks nonempty, not returned IDs or coordinate bounds. A client ignoring the predicate can pass those checks when the raw server filter remains correct. OWSLib has stronger exact-set checks.
findings.recommendation: Assert exact GDAL output ID/name sets, known excluded rows and coordinate bounds, plus deliberately ignored-filter controls. Retain GDAL-specific evidence rather than replacing it with raw HTTP or OWSLib.

declared_routes.shard: FeatureServer Endpoints Query Services and Replication

selection.execution_caveat: CI composes shard filters excluding Fast/Slow. Fast protocol projects are covered by foundation tests; Slow belongs to distinct workflow. Static declaration is not proof a current run executed matching tests. Existing NC10 owns no-tests success; not duplicated here.

limits: No runtime defect reproduced or new issue filed. Prior closed regression issue references are context, not current unassigned implementation claims.
Existing NC01–12 are not refiled; in particular OWSLib expired-token NC07, DuckDB CRS NC12 and shard no-test NC10 retain their owners.
No complete claim for all CRS/Z/M shapes, true-curve preservation, concurrency races, canonical-client writes, media variants, or tenant isolation follows from the sampled tests.
No fresh candidate or AWS qualification; no current CITE rate inferred from source. STAC/gRPC not expanded in this bounded pass.
